description: Abfahrten oder Ankünfte für EINE Haltestelle — **als Daten, für Ergebnisse, die du weiterverarbeitest**. Steht `show_departures` in deinem Werkzeug-Satz, ist das der Vordereingang für die Frage eines Menschen. Für „wann fährt von X", „letzte Stadtbahn von X" kommt die Auskunft aus diesen Werkzeugen; für eine A→B-Frage aus `connections`. **Pflicht** ist eine konkrete Stop-`id` aus einer vorhergehenden Ortsauflösung (z.B. `'de:03241:57'`); ein Haltestellen-NAME in `id` ist ein Argument-Fehler, keine leere Tafel. **Optional**: `time` und `is_arrival_time`; `modes` (Flüge `['air']`, ohne sie `['transit']`); `direction` (Halt-Name, in dessen Richtung gefahren wird) bzw. für eine weiche Angabe `target_bearing` mit `bearing_tolerance`; `lines` (Linie oder Linie@Richtung, wie die Tafel sie an `mot.line.direction.ids` nennt); `arrival_departure`; ein Fenster `time_range_seconds` mit `last_of_window`; und für den Umfang `verbosity`, `limit` sowie `render_payload`. Für „letzte Bahn heute", „erste S-Bahn morgen" statt der Tafel `first_last`: je Linie und Richtung erste und letzte Fahrt des Tages (`time` wählt den Tag). Für „hat X einen Aufzug zur U-Bahn?" statt der Tafel `facilities`: Aufzüge, Rolltreppen, Rampen des Halts. `modes`, `lines` und `direction` schränken hart ein. **Eine leere Tafel ist keine Auskunft**: blieb sie mit `['tram']` („Straßenbahn") leer, mit `['tram','subway']` nachfassen — sonst ohne den Filter. **Namen** in `lang` (Vorgabe `'de'`), der Name vor Ort daneben in `localName` — „Meran (Merano)". **Anleitung**: `get_usage_guide` mit `tool='departures'` — erste und letzte Fahrt, Aufzüge, die Echtzeit-, Ausfall- und Zitier-Felder. **Anti-Fab**: Linien, Richtungen, Zeiten, Gleise, Verspätung, Ausfall und Aufzüge ausschließlich aus dem Output dieses Aufrufs.

inputSchema.description:
A departure board for one stop. `Default` is derived for the same reason as
on [`ConnectionRequest`].

arrival_departure.description:
`"arrivals"` (when vehicles reach `id`) or `"departures"` (default) — a
third value is an argument error. Wins over `is_arrival_time` when both
are set.

bearing_tolerance.description: Angular tolerance in degrees for `target_bearing`. Default ±60°.

direction.description:
Name of a stop the user wants to head TOWARD („Richtung Wettbergen") —
not a routing destination. The board keeps only departures heading that
way, whether the named stop is the terminus or a stop downstream of the
queried one. Matching is case-insensitive and area-prefix-tolerant.

extended.description:
`true` keeps the map data in the text: every stop's coordinate, the whole
course of each run, and each departure's way (`pathOnMap`, `pathSource`,
`additionalInfos.pathKind`) — for an application that DRAWS the board. It
multiplies the answer. A chat client leaves it off.

facilities.description:
Instead of the board, the stop's lifts, escalators and ramps („hat Kröpcke einen Aufzug
zur U-Bahn?"): `"elevator"`, `"escalator"`, `"ramp"` or `"all"`; the guide has the fields.

first_last.description:
`true` answers instead of the board, per line and direction, the first and the last
ride of a day („letzte Bahn heute"): the day running now, or the calendar day of `time`
in local time.

format.description:
Answer serialisation: `"toon"` (default) or `"json"` — the detail is in
`get_usage_guide`. **An agent leaves this out.**

id.description:
Stop id to read the board of, as the resolver hands it out: a DHID (`"de:03241:57"`,
`at:…`, `ch:…`, `it:…`) or a station id (`"Parentch:1:sloid:3000"`). Resolve the stop first — a
name here is an argument error.

is_arrival_time.description:
`true` reads `time` as an ARRIVAL time — the same as
`arrival_departure = "arrivals"`.

lang.description: Die Sprache der Namen: `'de'` (Vorgabe), `'it'`, `'fr'`, auch mit Region (`'de-CH'`).

last_of_window.description:
Which end of a `time_range_seconds` window to read: omitted or `false` the
FIRST departures, `true` the LAST ones (the end-of-service question). An
answer carrying `window_truncated: true` beside its board did NOT reach the
window's end — its last entry is then not the last departure. Without a
window it has no effect.

limit.description:
Maximum number of departures, at least 1. Default 5, values above 15 are
served as 15.

lines.description:
Only the departures of these lines, by the ids a board writes: the line alone
(either direction) as at `mot.line.id`, or line@direction as at
`mot.line.direction.ids` (`"de:VBN-VH:6002:_3@0"`); several combine. A line
NUMBER (`"9"`) is no id — read the id off a board first. An entry that is no line
is an argument error.

modes.description:
Transport-mode filter; the board then shows nothing else. Entries:
`"bus"`, `"tram"`, `"subway"`, `"train"`/`"rail"`, `"ferry"`, `"air"`
(flights), `"transit"` (all of them but flights); several combine. Another entry — a street mode, a misspelling
— is an argument error, not a dropped filter: a board lists scheduled
services. Omitted or empty = all modes. A Stadtbahn or
light-rail mention needs BOTH labels — `["tram","subway"]`: which of the
two such a network carries depends on the dataset rather than on the
vehicle. Set the filter only when the user really asks for a vehicle type;
the guide has the rest of the vocabulary and the traps.

render_payload.description:
`true` appends the same board again as raw JSON, addressed to the user
rather than to the model — for an application that draws a departure
board. A chat client leaves this off: it is the whole answer twice.

target_bearing.description:
Target bearing in degrees (0=N, 90=E, 180=S, 270=W) for a SOFT direction
(„Richtung Norden", „Richtung Stadt") instead of a stop name. The board
keeps only departures whose course lies within `bearing_tolerance` of it.
Mutually exclusive with `direction`.

time.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. `"2026-06-15T08:30:00Z"`). Omit for now. Resolve
a spoken time with the time tool rather than computing one.

time_range_seconds.description:
Time WINDOW in seconds, starting at `time`. Together with `last_of_window`
it reads the last rides before the window ends: pick it so the window ENDS
where the question does. The last ride of a day is `first_last`. Omit for a
normal next-N lookup.

verbosity.description:
How much of each departure comes back: `"compact"` (default — everything
an answer is cited from) or `"full"` (adds the onward stops of the run,
and with them the per-stop cancellation marker). A third word is an
argument error, not the default.
